title: Threat-model an IIoT edge node before you write the updater
objective: Produce a threat model for a simulated IIoT edge node with at least six assets, four attacker positions, one specific mitigation per asset, a trust-boundary diagram, and an explicit unsigned-or-rollback firmware threat tied to RFC 9019.
whyThisMatters: OTA without a threat model is how nodes get bricked or owned. RFC 9019 names the firmware-update problem; this task is where you write the assets and boundaries so the next task's dual-slot design is answering a list, not a vibe.
evidence: THREAT.md listing at least six assets, at least four attacker positions, and one specific mitigation per asset
A data-flow or trust-boundary diagram (Mermaid or an ASCII figure) in THREAT.md that names at least two trust boundaries
A section that names an unsigned or roll-backable firmware image as a threat and a mitigation that names both signing and a freshness or anti-rollback check, citing RFC 9019 by section or quote
Git history showing THREAT.md drafted before any updater code (the updater is the next task)
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: THREAT.md lists at least six assets and at least four attacker positions (for example: local bus, physical debug, uplink MITM, malicious update server).

Each of the six assets has a mitigation that names a mechanism (for example HMAC on telemetry, disable SWD in production, TLS-PSK, signed image) — not the phrase 'use security' or 'encrypt everything' alone.
The diagram names at least two trust boundaries (for example sensor-bus vs MCU, MCU vs uplink).
One threat is an unsigned or version-downgraded firmware image; its mitigation names signing and a freshness or anti-rollback check and cites RFC 9019 (section number or a quoted sentence).
